Ui.Script:
-- The naming contract every verb below rests on: an "item button" is a Button whose own -- name prefixes its regions — `<name>IconTexture`, `<name>Count`, `<name>Stock`, -- `<name>NormalTexture`, `<name>NameFrame`, `<name>SlotTexture`. That is the reference's -- `$parent…` template shape, and it is why these are free functions taking a button rather -- than widget methods: any button that follows the naming works, whoever built it. -- -- Nil guards are the REFERENCE's, not ours — one on `button` per verb, and one on the icon -- region in SetItemButtonDesaturated. A missing region anywhere else raises, and that is -- the right loudness: "this is not an item button" is a real mistake, and 1203's lesson is -- that the silent version of a failure is the expensive one.
function SetItemButtonCount(button, count) if not button then return end if not count then count = 0 end button.count = count -- `isBag` is the reference's own flag for a bag button, where even a single item -- counts as a number worth showing. if count > 1 or (button.isBag and count > 0) then if count > 999 then count = "*" end getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Count"):SetText(count) getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Count"):Show() else getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Count"):Hide() end end
function SetItemButtonStock(button, numInStock) if not button then return end -- The reference defaults this to `""` and then compares it with `> 0`, which is a -- string/number comparison Lua refuses — a raise on the only path the default can -- reach. Ours defaults to 0, which is what the branch below actually means. Not aping -- a quirk (method step 3); the behaviour on every reachable path is identical. if not numInStock then numInStock = 0 end button.numInStock = numInStock if numInStock > 0 then getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Stock"):SetText(format(MERCHANT_STOCK, numInStock)) getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Stock"):Show() else getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Stock"):Hide() end end
function SetItemButtonTexture(button, texture) if not button then return end -- Show/Hide FIRST, then SetTexture — the reference's order, and it matters: a nil -- texture hides the region rather than leaving an empty quad behind. if texture then getglobal(button:GetName() .. "IconTexture"):Show() else getglobal(button:GetName() .. "IconTexture"):Hide() end getglobal(button:GetName() .. "IconTexture"):SetTexture(texture) end
function SetItemButtonTextureVertexColor(button, r, g, b) if not button then return end getglobal(button:GetName() .. "IconTexture"):SetVertexColor(r, g, b) end
function SetItemButtonDesaturated(button, desaturated, r, g, b) if not button then return end local icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "IconTexture") if not icon then return end -- The reference asks the texture itself whether the desaturating shader is available -- (`local shaderSupported = icon:SetDesaturated(desaturated)`) and falls through to a -- flat grey tint when it is not — 1.12 ran on fixed-function hardware where that was -- the ordinary answer. benilla has no `Texture:SetDesaturated` at all (it is the top -- row of the harness's missing-METHODS ranking, 61 corpus addons), so the feature test -- is on the METHOD's existence and the no-shader branch is the one we take. When the -- real verb lands this line starts using it with nothing else to change. local shaderSupported = icon.SetDesaturated and icon:SetDesaturated(desaturated) if not desaturated then r = 1.0 g = 1.0 b = 1.0 elseif not r or not shaderSupported then r = 0.5 g = 0.5 b = 0.5 end icon:SetVertexColor(r, g, b) end
function SetItemButtonNormalTextureVertexColor(button, r, g, b) if not button then return end getglobal(button:GetName() .. "NormalTexture"):SetVertexColor(r, g, b) end
function SetItemButtonNameFrameVertexColor(button, r, g, b) if not button then return end getglobal(button:GetName() .. "NameFrame"):SetVertexColor(r, g, b) end
function SetItemButtonSlotVertexColor(button, r, g, b) if not button then return end getglobal(button:GetName() .. "SlotTexture"):SetVertexColor(r, g, b) end
